value.body: Food processing and agri-business companies buy farm produce, process and package it, and sell it through supply chains. Agriculture graduates commonly work in procurement (sourcing from farmers and mandis), quality assurance, field operations, warehousing and supply chain, and agri-input or commodity sales.

items.label: Food safety regulator
items.note: Under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006

items.label: Typical entry roles
items.value: Procurement, quality assurance, field and supply-chain executive

items.note: Food processing's share of total employment in registered (organised) manufacturing

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A B.Sc Agriculture is usually enough for entry roles, through campus placements or direct applications. Food-technology training helps for quality posts. An MBA or PG diploma in agri-business management leads to management-trainee tracks; those programmes have their own admission tests.

value.title: At a glance
items: Many roles are field-based — plants, collection centres and rural areas — especially early on.
Quality roles need working knowledge of FSSAI standards and food-safety systems.
Growth often leads to supply-chain, category or plant management.
